Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.

# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate`, starts a game for a quiz, and shows the big screen. The audience joins
on their phones with a link or QR code, answers the questions live, and sees the
results. When the quiz ends, the big screen shows the leaderboard, the moderator picks the
winners (Top N, Draw, Reset winners), and each phone shows its place and whether it won.
Quizzes can be exported and imported as JSON.

## Run it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
    SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
    bin/serve

`bin/serve` prepares the database and assets and runs the app in the foreground.
All data is kept under `storage/`. `GET /up` answers 200 when the app is ready.

## Tests

    bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
    bin/rails test:system   # browser tests (Chromium, via Cuprite), including live games

`bin/rails test:system` starts several browser sessions: the big screen and phones.
It takes about 30 seconds.

Design notes, routes, and decisions are in `docs/design-notes.md` (see "Live game").
Design files are in `docs/mockups/`.
---
# Quizzy: design notes

Notes for whoever builds the next release. The live game (big screen, phones) is in "Live game".
The design files live in `docs/mockups/` (style guide, quiz page, question form).

## Running it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve

`bin/serve` creates or migrates the SQLite databases (`db:prepare`), precompiles
assets (`assets:precompile`, digests into `public/assets`), and then runs Puma in
the foreground on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`. It exits with an error if one of the three
required variables is missing.

- All data lives in `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (quizzes), `production_cache`,
  `production_queue` and `production_cable` (Solid Cache/Queue/Cable, unused so far).
- Logs go to STDOUT (default production logging). Nothing calls external services.
- Plain HTTP, no `force_ssl`, no host allow-list (`config.hosts` is empty in production).
- `GET /up` returns 200 without credentials.

## Routes and access

Everything under `/moderate` goes through `Moderate::BaseController`, which runs
HTTP Basic auth first. Unset, wrong, or empty credentials give 401 with
`WWW-Authenticate`. Unknown `/moderate/*` URLs also ask for credentials before
returning 404, so the route table does not leak to anonymous visitors.
The comparison uses `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.

| Page | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Quiz list, "New quiz" | `GET /moderate` (`moderate_root`) |
| New quiz / save | `GET /moderate/quizzes/new`, `POST /moderate/quizzes` |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Settings (quiz form) and "Delete quiz" | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:id` |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` |
| Export (quiz as JSON in a `<pre>`) | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` |
| Import page / import (always a new quiz) | `GET /moderate/imports/new`, `POST /moderate/imports` |
| New / edit question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new`, `…/:id/edit` |
| Save question, delete | `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions[/:id]` |
| Move up / down | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/move?direction=up|down` |
| Active checkbox | `PATCH /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/:id/activation` |

## Data model

- `Quiz`: `title` (required), `winner_count` (whole number, at least 1, default 3; the
  "Number of winners" field in the quiz settings, see "Prizes").
- `Question`: `quiz_id`, `text` (required), `position` (1-based, per quiz), `active`
  (default true). Inactive questions stay in the order. Numbering on the quiz page
  ("1", "2", …) counts active questions only; inactive ones show "—".
- `Option`: `question_id`, `text`, `correct`, `position`.

### Option rules (`Question`)

- Rows whose text is blank after `strip` are skipped",
  "output_tail": "set_winners` in `app/models/game.rb`, and the finished-phase markup in
`moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` and `play/_screen.html.erb`.

### Scoring and speed

- A point is one correct answer (any correct option). A player who changes a pick is scored
  on the last pick.
- Speed breaks ties. A correct answer's time runs from `game_questions.opened_at` (set by the
  server when the question opened) to `answers.picked_at` (the player's last pick). A player's
  total is the sum over their correct answers, in integer microseconds (`time_us`), so sums
  never depend on float rounding. Wrong answers add no time. The lower total ranks higher.
- Order: points (most first), total time (least first), then join order. The join order only
  decides how tied players are listed.
- Places are competition ranks: players with the same points and total share a place, so
  the places read 1, 2, 2, 4. Players with no points share the last place.
- Everyone who joined is on the leaderboard, including players with no answers.
- Points and places are computed only after the end. During the game the phones show no
  points, and the big screen shows only answer counts.

### Winners

- **Top N**: the first N players of the leaderboard who have at least one point.
- **Draw**: the N-th entry of the scoring list gives the threshold. Players with more points
  than the threshold win. The remaining prizes are drawn at random (`Array#sample`) among the
  players with exactly the threshold's points, speed ignored. Each click draws again.
- If fewer than N players have points, all of them win. Players with 0 points never win.
- **Reset winners** clears every winner flag.
- Every pick replaces the previous winners: the flags are cleared and set in one transaction.
- Picks only work after the end. The update matches `finished_at IS NOT NULL` and bumps
  `state_version`, the same guard style as the other transitions. A pick before the end says
  "End the quiz before picking winners."
- A successful pick with nobody holding points says "Nobody has points yet, so there are no
  winners."
- N is read from the quiz each time a button is pressed, so a settings change applies to the
  next pick. `GameScreen#version` includes N, so the "Top N" label follows the setting on the
  next poll.
- Each pick sends one refresh to the big screen and one to the phones, as the other
  transitions do. The marks arrive live, with no data in the signal.

### What the screens show

- **Big screen** after End quiz: `ol.leaderboard` with one `li.leader` per player. Each
  item has the place, the name, "N points" (`pluralize`), and a "Winner" badge for winners
  (`is-winner`, from the design's leaderboard styles). The control bar gets "Top N", "Draw"
  and "Reset winners".
- **Phone** after End quiz: "Place P of T" and "N points". Winners also see "You won!"
  (`winner-banner`). A phone that never joined sees only "The quiz is over".
- The "Number of winners" field is in the quiz form, which also serves "New quiz". It has
  `min="1"`, so a browser blocks 0, and the model refuses 0 and non-integers as well.

### Export and import

The JSON export keeps its documented keys (`title`, `questions`), so it does not include the
number of winners. An import creates a quiz with the default of 3. If the number should travel
with the quiz, add it to `QuizExport` and `QuizImport` and update the key list above.

## Testing

    bin/rails test                 # models and integration (Capybara rack_test)
    bin/rails test:system          # browser tests with Cuprite and /usr/bin/chromium
    bin/rubocop
    bin/brakeman -q

The system tests use `BROWSER_PATH` (defaults to `/usr/bin/chromium`) and run with
`--no-sandbox`, which the container needs. Moderator credentials in tests are set in
`test/test_helper.rb`.
The prize rules are covered by `test/models/leaderboard_test.rb` (points, speed, places,
Top N and Draw, with `travel_to` for exact times), `test/models/game_prizes_test.rb` (the
guards, the replacement of winners, the signals), `test/integration/prizes_test.rb` (the
pages, the buttons, the phones) and `test/system/prizes_browser_test.rb` (a whole game in
four browser sessions).

## Open points for later releases

- Results across games: a leaderboard or per-quiz statistics. The `runs-table` and
  `response-*` styles are in the stylesheet but unused. The game's leaderboard uses the
  `leader*` styles (see "Prizes").
- A moderator "Remove player" or leave action, if the active-player count should
  ever differ from the number of joined players.
- `brakeman` reports a Ruby 3.4.4 CVE (`.ruby-version`). The environment is fixed at
  3.4.4, so this is noted and not changed.
- `bin/bundler-audit` needs the advisory database from GitHub. It cannot run without
  network access.

# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate`, starts a game for a quiz, and shows the big screen. The audience joins
on their phones with a link or QR code, answers the questions live, and sees the
results. When the quiz ends, the big screen shows the leaderboard, the moderator picks the
winners (Top N, Draw, Reset winners), and each phone shows its place and whether it won.
Quizzes can be exported and imported as JSON.

## Run it

    RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
    SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
    QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
    bin/serve

`bin/serve` prepares the database and assets and runs the app in the foreground.
All data is kept under `storage/`. `GET /up` answers 200 when the app is ready.

## Tests

    bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
    bin/rails test:system   # browser tests (Chromium, via Cuprite), including live games

`bin/rails test:system` starts several browser sessions: the big screen and phones.
It takes about 30 seconds.

Design notes, routes, and decisions are in `docs/design-notes.md` (see "Live game").
Design files are in `docs/mockups/`.

### Scoring and speed

- A point is one correct answer (any correct option). A player who changes a pick is scored
  on the last pick.
- Speed breaks ties. A correct answer's time runs from `game_questions.opened_at` (set by the
  server when the question opened) to `answers.picked_at` (the player's last pick). A player's
  total is the sum over their correct answers, in integer microseconds (`time_us`), so sums
  never depend on float rounding. Wrong answers add no time. The lower total ranks higher.
- Order: points (most first), total time (least first), then join order. The join order only
  decides how tied players are listed.
- Places are competition ranks: players with the same points and total share a place, so
  the places read 1, 2, 2, 4. Players with no points share the last place.
- Everyone who joined is on the leaderboard, including players with no answers.
- Points and places are computed only after the end. During the game the phones show no
  points, and the big screen shows only answer counts.

### Winners

- **Top N**: the first N players of the leaderboard who have at least one point.
- **Draw**: the N-th entry of the scoring list gives the threshold. Players with more points
  than the threshold win. The remaining prizes are drawn at random (`Array#sample`) among the
  players with exactly the threshold's points, speed ignored. Each click draws again.
- If fewer than N players have points, all of them win. Players with 0 points never win.
- **Reset winners** clears every winner flag.
- Every pick replaces the previous winners: the flags are cleared and set in one transaction.
- Picks only work after the end. The update matches `finished_at IS NOT NULL` and bumps
  `state_version`, the same guard style as the other transitions. A pick before the end says
  "End the quiz before picking winners."
- A successful pick with nobody holding points says "Nobody has points yet, so there are no
  winners."
- N is read from the quiz each time a button is pressed, so a settings change applies to the
  next pick. `GameScreen#version` includes N, so the "Top N" label follows the setting on the
  next poll.
- Each pick sends one refresh to the big screen and one to the phones, as the other
  transitions do. The marks arrive live, with no data in the signal.

### What the screens show

- **Big screen** after End quiz: `ol.leaderboard` with one `li.leader` per player. Each
  item has the place, the name, "N points" (`pluralize`), and a "Winner" badge for winners
  (`is-winner`, from the design's leaderboard styles). The control bar gets "Top N", "Draw"
  and "Reset winners".
- **Phone** after End quiz: "Place P of T" and "N points". Winners also see "You won!"
  (`winner-banner`). A phone that never joined sees only "The quiz is over".
- The "Number of winners" field is in the quiz form, which also serves "New quiz". It has
  `min="1"`, so a browser blocks 0, and the model refuses 0 and non-integers as well.

### Export and import

The JSON export keeps its documented keys (`title`, `questions`), so it does not include the
number of winners. An import creates a quiz with the default of 3. If the number should travel
with the quiz, add it to `QuizExport` and `QuizImport` and update the key list above.

    bin/rails test                 # models and integration (Capybara rack_test)
    bin/rails test:system          # browser tests with Cuprite and /usr/bin/chromium

The system tests use `BROWSER_PATH` (defaults to `/usr/bin/chromium`) and run with
`--no-sandbox`, which the container needs. Moderator credentials in tests are set in
`test/test_helper.rb`.
The prize rules are covered by `test/models/leaderboard_test.rb` (points, speed, places,
Top N and Draw, with `travel_to` for exact times), `test/models/game_prizes_test.rb` (the

copying JSON. There is no file upload or download: both sides are plain text.

  `QuizExport` writes pretty-printed JSON into one `<pre class="code-block export-json">`

  exactly `title` and `questions`; each question has `text`, `active`, `options`; each

  exported too, and questions and options keep their order.
- **Import**: the "Import quiz" button on `/moderate` opens `/moderate/imports/new`
  with the "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. `QuizImport` always creates
  a new quiz (titles are not matched), then redirects to its page with "Quiz imported.".

  counts as left out. Unknown keys are ignored.
- **Types are strict**: `title`, question `text` and option `text` must be strings;
  `active` and `correct` must be true or false; `questions` and `options` must be
  lists; each question and option must be an object. A wrong shape gives one message
  such as "Questions must be a list.", with 422.

  and quiz title are required; blank option rows are skipped (a correct box on a blank
  row does not count); at least two filled options; at least one correct. The messages
  are the models' messages, prefixed with the question's place in the JSON, for example
  "Question 2: Add at least two options". The locale names the question text
  "Question", so the blank case reads "Question 2: Question can't be blank", as the
  form does.

  calls one `quiz.save`. That validates the quiz and every question before any insert,
  and runs in one transaction. A failed import writes nothing, and the page re-renders
  with 422 and the pasted text.
- **Parse errors**: blank input gives "Paste the quiz JSON to import."; invalid JSON
  gives "The quiz JSON is not valid JSON: ..." with the parser's message. A leading
  byte-order mark is ignored.
- Code: `app/models/quiz_export.rb`, `app/models/quiz_import.rb`,
  `app/controllers/moderate/imports_controller.rb`, views in `moderate/quizzes/export`
  and `moderate/imports/new`. Tests: `test/models/quiz_export_test.rb`,
  `test/models/quiz_import_test.rb`, `test/integration/quiz_transfer_test.rb`,
  `test/system/quiz_transfer_browser_test.rb`.

## Form and UI decisions

- **Option rows**: `question[options][i][text]` and `question[options][i][correct]`
  (checkbox value `1`). A new question, or an edit with fewer than four options,
  shows four rows (`ApplicationHelper::FORM_OPTION_ROWS`).
- **Labels**: the row text field has a visually hidden `<label>` "Option N". The
  checkbox label reads "Option N is correct" (the visible word is just "correct",
  the context is a visually hidden prefix). Visible labels follow the design.
- **"Add option"** is a submit button (`name="add_option"`) with `formnovalidate`.
  The server re-renders the form with one more row, keeping the typed values. No
  JavaScript is needed for that.
- **Enter key**: the first submit button in the form is a hidden empty button, so
  Enter in an option field saves the question and does not trigger "Add option".
- **Active checkbox on the quiz page**: a tiny Stimulus controller
  (`auto_submit_controller.js`) calls `requestSubmit()` on change. The form has its
  own `activation` route, so it cannot touch the question text or options.
- **Confirmations** ("Delete" question, "Delete quiz") use Turbo's
  `data-turbo-confirm`, which calls the browser's native `confirm()`.
- **Redirects after POST/PATCH/DELETE** use `303 See Other`, so Turbo follows them
  with GET.
- The question and quiz forms set `data-turbo="false"` because they re-render with
  422/200 on errors and a plain form post is simpler to reason about.
- **Move up / Move down** stay enabled at the ends (the first item's "Move up" is
  dimmed with `is-edge`). A move past an end is a no-op.
- **"Add question"** and **"New quiz"** are buttons that submit a GET form to the
  new-record page, so they are `<button>`s as the brief says.
- The correct option chips on the quiz page get the design's ✓ (from CSS) and a
  visually hidden "(correct)", so screen readers hear the mark too.

## Preview: stateless by design

`QuizPreview` (app/models/quiz_preview.rb) plays the quiz using only URL parameters,
so nothing is written to the database:

- `answers=<id>,<id>,…`: option ids picked so far, one per active question, in order.
- `pick=<id>`: the option the participant just picked. The page then reveals the answer.

`finished`. The moderator buttons follow the state of the current question:

| State of the current question | Big screen shows | Button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lobby | title, join link (text), QR code, `Players: N` | Start |
| open | `Question i of n`, question, options, `Answers: x / y` | Finish |
| closed, not last | options with answer counts, `Correct` marks | Next |
| closed, last | same | End quiz |
| finished | `The quiz is over`, the leaderboard (see "Prizes") | Top N, Draw, Reset winners |

after the last question has closed.

### Routes

| Page | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Start a game (from the quiz page) | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games`, then redirect to the big screen |
| Big screen | `GET /moderate/games/:id` (moderator login) |
| Big screen fragment (for the live controller) | `GET /moderate/games/:id/screen` |
| Start / Finish / Next / End quiz | `POST /moderate/games/:id/{start,finish,next_question,end_quiz}` |
| Top N / Draw / Reset winners (after the end) | `POST /moderate/games/:id/{top_winners,draw_winners,reset_winners}` |
| Join link (phones, public) | `GET /play/:code`, `POST /play/:code/join` |
| Phone fragment (for the live controller) | `GET /play/:code/state` |
| Tap an option | `POST /play/:code/answer` (`option_id`) |

### Data model

- `Game`: `quiz_id`, `code` (unique), `current_position` (0 in the lobby, else the
  1-based game question on screen), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `state_version`.
- `GameQuestion` and `GameOption`: a **copy** of the quiz's active questions and options.

  questions are never copied, so games skip them.
- `Player`: `game_id`, `name` (squished, at most 40 characters), `token` (random, unique),
  `winner` (boolean, set only by the prize buttons, see "Prizes").
- `Answer`: one row per player and game question (unique index). Picking again updates it,
  and `picked_at` moves to the new pick. `picked_at` is the time for the speed tie-break.

with a message. `state_version` goes up on every change.

checks that the question is still open. Finish takes the same lock, so no pick can land

question is open, so the markup has no way to show it. The open-question phone page

cannot leak either.

  commits.

  owns one region (`#game-screen` or `#player-screen`). On a signal, or on its timer, it
  fetches the region's HTML and swaps it in if the `data-live-version-value` changed.
  Each phone fetches its own state with its cookie, so no one sees another player's pick.
  The server answers `304` when the version has not changed (ETag).

steps took 250-450 ms.

### Gotchas

  `test_helper.rb` includes `Turbo::Broadcastable::TestHelper`. Use
  `assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts ..., count: 0` to assert that nothing was sent.
- A flex container splits its children into separate lines in the browser's text. A
  label and a number in separate elements inside `.counter-pill` read "Players:" and "2"
  on separate lines. Keep the label and the number in one inline element (see the
  `counter-pill` in `app/views/moderate/games/_screen.html.erb`).
- The row objects for the screens (`GameScreen::Row`, `PlayerScreen::Row`) are built
  with `correct` set to `nil` until it is revealed, so a partial cannot print a flag
  that was never revealed.

### Decisions

- A game copies the quiz when it starts, not when it is created. The lobby can wait for
  players while the moderator fixes a typo in a question. "Start a game" refuses when
  the quiz has no active question, and so does Start, with a message.
- "Players" means everyone who joined the game. Nobody can leave or be removed, so
  the answer counter's denominator is the number of joined players. Players who join
  after the start count too.
- The join link on the big screen is built from the request host
  (`http://host:port/play/CODE`). Open the big screen through an address the phones can
  reach, for example the LAN address.
- The phone's player is kept in a signed, permanent cookie named after the code
  (`quizzy_player_CODE`). Clearing cookies creates a new player.
- Quiz deletion deletes its games, players and answers.
- The QR code is an inline SVG made by `rqrcode` (in the Gemfile). No CDN and no
  JavaScript library, so the app works offline.

## Prizes

Once a game has ended, the moderator picks the winners on the big screen. The number of
prizes is the quiz setting "Number of winners" (`quizzes.winner_count`, default 3). Code:
`app/models/leaderboard.rb` (standings and winner rules), `Game#pick_top_winners`,
`#draw_winners`, `#reset_winners` in `app/models/game.rb`, and the finished-phase markup in
`moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` and `play/_screen.html.erb`.

### Scoring and speed

- A point is one correct answer (any correct option). A player who changes a pick is scored
  on the last pick.
- Speed breaks ties. A correct answer's time runs from `game_questions.opened_at` (set by the
  server when the question opened) to `answers.picked_at` (the player's last pick). A player's
  total is the sum over their correct answers, in integer microseconds (`time_us`), so sums
  never depend on float rounding. Wrong answers add no time. The lower total ranks higher.
- Order: points (most first), total time (least first), then join order. The join order only
  decides how tied players are listed.
- Places are competition ranks: players with the same points and total share a place, so
  the places read 1, 2, 2, 4. Players with no points share the last place.
- Everyone who joined is on the leaderboard, including players with no answers.
- Points and places are computed only after the end. During the game the phones show no
  points, and the big screen shows only answer counts.

### Winners

- **Top N**: the first N players of the leaderboard who have at least one point.
- **Draw**: the N-th entry of the scoring list gives the threshold. Players with more points
  than the threshold win. The remaining prizes are drawn at random (`Array#sample`) among the
  players with exactly the threshold's points, speed ignored. Each click draws again.
- If fewer than N players have points, all of them win. Players with 0 points never win.
- **Reset winners** clears every winner flag.
- Every pick replaces the previous winners: the flags are cleared and set in one transaction.
- Picks only work after the end. The update matches `finished_at IS NOT NULL` and bumps
  `state_version`, the same guard style as the other transitions. A pick before the end says
  "End the quiz before picking winners."
- A successful pick with nobody holding points says "Nobody has points yet, so there are no
  winners."
- N is read from the quiz each time a button is pressed, so a settings change applies to the
  next pick. `GameScreen#version` includes N, so the "Top N" label follows the setting on the
  next poll.
- Each pick sends one refresh to the big screen and one to the phones, as the other
  transitions do. The marks arrive live, with no data in the signal.

### What the screens show

- **Big screen** after End quiz: `ol.leaderboard` with one `li.leader` per player. Each
  item has the place, the name, "N points" (`pluralize`), and a "Winner" badge for winners
  (`is-winner`, from the design's leaderboard styles). The control bar gets "Top N", "Draw"
  and "Reset winners".
- **Phone** after End quiz: "Place P of T" and "N points". Winners also see "You won!"
  (`winner-banner`). A phone that never joined sees only "The quiz is over".
- The "Number of winners" field is in the quiz form, which also serves "New quiz". It has
  `min="1"`, so a browser blocks 0, and the model refuses 0 and non-integers as well.

### Export and import

The JSON export keeps its documented keys (`title`, `questions`), so it does not include the
number of winners. An import creates a quiz with the default of 3. If the number should travel
with the quiz, add it to `QuizExport` and `QuizImport` and update the key list above.

## Testing

    bin/rails test                 # models and integration (Capybara rack_test)
    bin/rails test:system          # browser tests with Cuprite and /usr/bin/chromium
    bin/rubocop
    bin/brakeman -q

The system tests use `BROWSER_PATH` (defaults to `/usr/bin/chromium`) and run with
`--no-sandbox`, which the container needs. Moderator credentials in tests are set in
`test/test_helper.rb`.
The prize rules are covered by `test/models/leaderboard_test.rb` (points, speed, places,
Top N and Draw, with `travel_to` for exact times), `test/models/game_prizes_test.rb` (the
guards, the replacement of winners, the signals), `test/integration/prizes_test.rb` (the
pages, the buttons, the phones) and `test/system/prizes_browser_test.rb` (a whole game in
four browser sessions).

## Open points for later releases

- Results across games: a leaderboard or per-quiz statistics. The `runs-table` and
  `response-*` styles are in the stylesheet but unused. The game's leaderboard uses the
  `leader*` styles (see "Prizes").
- A moderator "Remove player" or leave action, if the active-player count should
  ever differ from the number of joined players.
- `brakeman` reports a Ruby 3.4.4 CVE (`.ruby-version`). The environment is fixed at
  3.4.4, so this is noted and not changed.
- `bin/bundler-audit` needs the advisory database from GitHub. It cannot run without
  network access.

    bin/rails test:system          # browser tests with Cuprite and /usr/bin/chromium
    bin/rubocop
    bin/brakeman -q

The system tests use `BROWSER_PATH` (defaults to `/usr/bin/chromium`) and run with
`--no-sandbox`, which the container needs. Moderator credentials in tests are set in
`test/test_helper.rb`.
The prize rules are covered by `test/models/leaderboard_test.rb` (points, speed, places,
Top N and Draw, with `travel_to` for exact times), `test/models/game_prizes_test.rb` (the
guards, the replacement of winners, the signals), `test/integration/prizes_test.rb` (the
pages, the buttons, the phones) and `test/system/prizes_browser_test.rb` (a whole game in
four browser sessions).

## Open points for later releases

- Results across games: a leaderboard or per-quiz statistics. The `runs-table` and
  `response-*` styles are in the stylesheet but unused. The game's leaderboard uses the
  `leader*` styles (see "Prizes").
- A moderator "Remove player" or leave action, if the active-player count should
  ever differ from the number of joined players.
- `brakeman` reports a Ruby 3.4.4 CVE (`.ruby-version`). The environment is fixed at
  3.4.4, so this is noted and not changed.
- `bin/bundler-audit` needs the advisory database from GitHub. It cannot run without
  network access.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prepares Quizzy and runs it in production mode in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app writes lives under storage/ (the SQLite databases).
# Plain HTTP on all interfaces; no SSL and no host checks.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for variable in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!variable:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $variable must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log

# Creates storage/<env>.sqlite3 (plus the cache, queue and cable databases in
# production) and runs pending migrations. Safe to run on every start.
bin/rails db:prepare

# Digests the stylesheets, fonts and JavaScript into public/assets.
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT"
"
}

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  # Largest value the integer column holds.
  MAX_WINNER_COUNT = 2_147_483_647

  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz
  has_many :games, dependent: :destroy

  validates :title, presence: true
  validate :winner_count_rules

  def active_questions
    questions.where(active: true)
  end

  # Swaps a question with its neighbour. Inactive questions take part in the
  # ordering too, so moving past them is allowed. Returns false at the ends.
  def move_question(question, direction)
    ordered = Question.where(quiz_id: id).order(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |candidate| candidate.id == question.id }
    return false unless index

    target = case direction.to_s
    when "up" then index - 1
    when "down" then index + 1
    else return false
    end
    return false unless target.between?(0, ordered.size - 1)

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |candidate, position|
        candidate.update_column(:position, position) unless candidate.position == position
      end
    end
    true
  end

  private

  # The checks read the typed text, so "2.5" or "" is refused rather than rounded.
  def winner_count_rules
    typed = winner_count_before_type_cast.to_s.strip

    unless typed.match?(/\A[+-]?\d+\z/)
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be a whole number")
      return
    end

    if winner_count < 1
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be at least 1")
    elsif winner_count > MAX_WINNER_COUNT
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be at most #{MAX_WINNER_COUNT}")
    end
  end
end
=====question
class Question < ApplicationRecord
  # One row of the question form. Rows keep what the moderator typed, including
  # empty ones, so a failed save can show the form exactly as it was submitted.
  OptionRow = Struct.new(:text, :correct, keyword_init: true) do
    def empty_text? = text.to_s.strip.empty?
  end

  MIN_OPTIONS = 2

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  before_create :assign_position
  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :option_rules
  after_save :replace_options, if: :option_rows_assigned?

  # The option rows as shown in the form. Until they are assigned, the
  # question's saved options are used.
  def option_rows
    @option_rows ||= options.map { |option| OptionRow.new(text: option.text, correct: option.correct) }
  end

  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows_assigned = true
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      OptionRow.new(text: row.text.to_s, correct: row.correct ? true : false)
    end
  end

  def filled_option_rows
    option_rows.reject(&:empty_text?)
  end

  def option_rows_assigned?
    @option_rows_assigned == true
  end

  private

  def assign_position
    self.position = Question.where(quiz_id: quiz_id).maximum(:position).to_i + 1 if position.to_i.zero?
  end

  def option_rules
    filled = filled_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if filled.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") unless filled.any?(&:correct)
  end

  # Runs after validation has passed, so a rejected form never touches the
  # saved options. Empty rows are skipped.
  def replace_options
    options.destroy_all
    filled_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      options.create!(text: row.text.strip, correct: row.correct, position: position)
    end
    options.reset
  end
end
=====game
# One play of a quiz, with its own join code, players and answers. A quiz can be

  # Swaps a question with its neighbour. Inactive questions take part in the
  # ordering too, so moving past them is allowed. Returns false at the ends.
  def move_question(question, direction)
    ordered = Question.where(quiz_id: id).order(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |candidate| candidate.id == question.id }
    return false unless index

    target = case direction.to_s

    when "down" then index + 1

    end
    return false unless target.between?(0, ordered.size - 1)

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    transaction do

        candidate.update_column(:position, position) unless candidate.position == position
      end
    end
    true

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  # One row of the question form. Rows keep what the moderator typed, including
  # empty ones, so a failed save can show the form exactly as it was submitted.
  OptionRow = Struct.new(:text, :correct, keyword_init: true) do
    def empty_text? = text.to_s.strip.empty?
  end

  MIN_OPTIONS = 2

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  before_create :assign_position
  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :option_rules
  after_save :replace_options, if: :option_rows_assigned?

  # The option rows as shown in the form. Until they are assigned, the
  # question's saved options are used.
  def option_rows
    @option_rows ||= options.map { |option| OptionRow.new(text: option.text, correct: option.correct) }
  end

  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows_assigned = true
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      OptionRow.new(text: row.text.to_s, correct: row.correct ? true : false)
    end
  end

  def filled_option_rows
    option_rows.reject(&:empty_text?)
  end

  def option_rows_assigned?
    @option_rows_assigned == true
  end

    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if filled.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") unless filled.any?(&:correct)

  # saved options. Empty rows are skipped.
  def replace_options

    filled_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      options.create!(text: row.text.strip, correct: row.correct, position: position)
    end
    options.reset
  end

  # Everything under /moderate requires the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.
  class BaseController < ApplicationController
    REALM = "Quizzy moderator".freeze

    layout "moderate"
    before_action :require_moderator

    # Catch-all for unknown moderator URLs: 404, but only after authentication.
    def missing
      raise ActionController::RoutingError, "No route matches [#{request.method}] #{request.path}"
    end

    private

    def require_moderator
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic(REALM) do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    # Fails closed: unset credentials never match.
    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      username_matches = ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username)

    end
  end

class PlayController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_game
  before_action :set_player

    @screen = PlayerScreen.new(@game, @player)
  end

  def join
    if @game.finished?
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    if @player
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    player = @game.players.new(name: params[:name])
    if player.save
      cookies.permanent.signed[cookie_name] = { value: player.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
      @game.broadcast_screen_refresh
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      @join_error = player.errors[:name].first || "Enter your name"
      @screen = PlayerScreen.new(@game, nil)
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # The phone's own region, fetched by the live controller.
  def state
    view = PlayerScreen.new(@game, @player)
    render partial: "play/screen", locals: { screen: view } if stale?(etag: view.version)
  end

  # Tapping an option. Answers with a Turbo Stream that replaces the phone's view.
  def answer
    message = nil

    if @player.nil?
      message = "Join the quiz first."
    else
      option = GameOption.joins(:game_question).find_by(id: params[:option_id], game_questions: { game_id: @game.id })
      if option.nil?
        message = "That answer is not part of this question."
      elsif !@player.pick(option)
        message = @player.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
      end
    end

    respond_to do |format|
      format.turbo_stream do
        render turbo_stream: turbo_stream.replace(
          "player-screen",
          partial: "play/screen",
          locals: { screen: PlayerScreen.new(@game, @player), message: message }
        )
      end
      format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
    end
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.includes(:quiz).with_join_code(params[:code])
    render :missing, status: :not_found if @game.nil?
  end

  def set_player
    token = cookies.signed[cookie_name]
    @player = @game.players.find_by(token: token) if token.present?

require "application_system_test_case"

# What keeps the screens right when the socket misses a signal (crowded Wi-Fi).
class LiveFallbackBrowserTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Largest planet?", options: [ [ "Jupiter", true ], [ "Mars", false ] ])
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    @code = find(".lobby__url").text[%r{/play/(\w+)\z}, 1]
  end

  # Replaces the push handler, so a page only catches up through its own timer.
  def mute_signals
    execute_script("Turbo.StreamActions.live_refresh = function () {}")
  end

  def join_phone(name)
    Capybara.using_session(:phone) do
      visit "/play/#{@code}"
      fill_in "Your name", with: name
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, #{name}!"
    end
  end

  test "a phone that misses the signal still shows the question on its own timer" do
    join_phone("Alice")
    Capybara.using_session(:phone) { mute_signals }

    click_button "Start"
    Capybara.using_session(:phone) do
      assert_text "Largest planet?", wait: 12
    end
  end

  test "a big screen that misses the signal still counts answers on its own timer" do
    join_phone("Alice")
    mute_signals
    assert_text "Players: 1", wait: 12

    click_button "Start"
    Capybara.using_session(:phone) do
      click_button "Jupiter"
      assert_text "Your answer"
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1", wait: 12
  end

  test "a tap that never reaches the server says so on the phone" do
    join_phone("Alice")
    click_button "Start"

    Capybara.using_session(:phone) do
      assert_text "Largest planet?"
      # Turbo reports a request that never reached the server with this event on the form.
      execute_script(<<~JS)
        const form = [...document.querySelectorAll(".play-option-form")].find((f) => f.textContent.includes("Mars"))
        form.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("turbo:fetch-request-error", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
      JS
      assert_text "No connection. Nothing was sent. Try again."
      assert_button "Mars"
    end
  end
end
"
}

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz
    @first = build_question(@quiz, text: "First?", options: [ [ "Yes", true ], [ "No", false ] ])
    @second = build_question(@quiz, text: "Second?", options: [ [ "A", false ], [ "B", true ] ])
    @skipped = build_question(@quiz, text: "Skipped?", active: false)
    @game = @quiz.games.create!
  end

  test "a new game gets a five character join code from the readable alphabet" do
    assert_match Game::CODE_FORMAT, @game.code
    assert_equal 5, @game.code.length
    refute_match(/[ILO01]/, @game.code)
  end

  test "each game has its own code, even for the same quiz" do
    other = @quiz.games.create!
    refute_equal @game.code, other.code
  end

  test "a new game is in the lobby with no questions copied yet" do
    assert @game.lobby?
    refute @game.running?
    refute @game.finished?
    assert_equal 0, @game.total_questions
    assert_nil @game.current_game_question
    assert_equal "Waiting to start", @game.status_label
  end

  test "start copies only the active questions, in order, with their options" do
    assert @game.start

    assert_equal %w[First? Second?], @game.game_questions.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], @game.game_questions.map(&:position)
    assert_equal [ [ "Yes", true ], [ "No", false ] ], @game.game_questions.first.options.map { |o| [ o.text, o.correct ] }
    assert_equal 1, @game.current_position
    assert @game.running?
    assert_equal "Running", @game.status_label
  end

  test "start opens the first question and nothing else" do
    @game.start

    assert @game.game_questions.first.open?
    assert @game.game_questions.second.pending?
  end

  test "start without any active question is refused and leaves the game in the lobby" do
    @quiz.questions.update_all(active: false)

    refute @game.start
    assert_includes @game.errors.full_messages, "Activate at least one question before starting the game."
    assert @game.lobby?
    assert_equal 0, @game.game_questions.count
  end

  test "a game cannot be started twice" do
    @game.start

    refute @game.start
    assert_includes @game.errors.full_messages, "The quiz has already started."
  end

  test "finish closes the open question and next opens the following one" do
    @game.start

    assert @game.finish_question
    assert @game.question_closed?
    assert @game.current_game_question.closed?

    assert @game.next_question
    assert_equal 2, @game.current_position
    assert @game.question_open?
    assert @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed?
  end

  test "finish is refused when no question is open" do
    refute @game.finish_question

- **Settings:** `quizzes.timer_minutes` and `quizzes.timer_seconds` (integers, default 0), set in the quiz form.

- **Display:** the big screen counts down in M:SS. Phones get no timer. The export format doesn't change.

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  # Largest value the integer column holds.
  MAX_WINNER_COUNT = 2_147_483_647
  # The timer is per question: a day of minutes is far more than any talk needs.
  MAX_TIMER_MINUTES = 1_440
  MAX_TIMER_SECONDS = 59

  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz
  has_many :games, dependent: :destroy

  validates :title, presence: true
  validate :winner_count_rules
  validate :timer_rules

  def active_questions
    questions.where(active: true)
  end

  # Time per question, in seconds. 0 means no timer.
  def time_limit_seconds
    timer_minutes.to_i * 60 + timer_seconds.to_i
  end

  # Swaps a question with its neighbour. Inactive questions take part in the
  # ordering too, so moving past them is allowed. Returns false at the ends.
  def move_question(question, direction)
    ordered = Question.where(quiz_id: id).order(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |candidate| candidate.id == question.id }
    return false unless index

    target = case direction.to_s
    when "up" then index - 1
    when "down" then index + 1
    else return false
    end
    return false unless target.between?(0, ordered.size - 1)

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |candidate, position|
        candidate.update_column(:position, position) unless candidate.position == position
      end
    end
    true
  end

  private

  # The checks read the typed text, so "2.5" or "" is refused rather than rounded.
  def winner_count_rules
    typed = winner_count_before_type_cast.to_s.strip

    unless typed.match?(/\A[+-]?\d+\z/)
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be a whole number")
      return
    end

    if winner_count < 1
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be at least 1")
    elsif winner_count > MAX_WINNER_COUNT
      errors.add(:winner_count, "must be at most #{MAX_WINNER_COUNT}")
    end
  end

  def timer_rules
    check_timer_field(:timer_minutes, MAX_TIMER_MINUTES)
    check_timer_field(:timer_seconds, MAX_TIMER_SECONDS)
  end

  # Same typed-text rule as the winner count: a blank or fractional value is refused.
  def check_timer_field(attribute, largest)
    typed = public_send(:"#{attribute}_before_type_cast").to_s.strip

    unless typed.match?(/\A[+-]?\d+\z/)
      errors.add(attribute, "must be a whole number")
      return
    end

    value = public_send(attribute)
    if value < 0
      errors.add(attribute, "must be at least 0")
    elsif value > largest
      errors.add(attribute, "must be at most #{largest}")
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class QuizTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "a new quiz has no timer: 0 minutes and 0 seconds" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk")

    assert_equal 0, quiz.timer_minutes
    assert_equal 0, quiz.timer_seconds
    assert_equal 0, quiz.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the time per question is minutes and seconds added up" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)

    assert_equal 90, quiz.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "a quiz with a timer saves, and its timer comes back from the database" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: 2, timer_seconds: 5)

    assert_equal 125, Quiz.find(quiz.id).time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "seconds must stay within a minute" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_seconds: 60)

    refute quiz.valid?
    assert_includes quiz.errors.full_messages, "Timer seconds must be at most 59"
  end

  test "the timer fields cannot be negative" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: -1, timer_seconds: -5)

    refute quiz.valid?
    assert_includes quiz.errors.full_messages, "Timer minutes must be at least 0"
    assert_includes quiz.errors.full_messages, "Timer seconds must be at least 0"
  end

  test "fractions, text and blanks are refused rather than rounded" do
    [ "1.5", "abc", "", "1e3" ].each do |typed|
      quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: typed)

      refute quiz.valid?, "expected #{typed.inspect} to be refused"
      assert_includes quiz.errors.full_messages, "Timer minutes must be a whole number"
    end
  end

  test "minutes have an upper limit" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: Quiz::MAX_TIMER_MINUTES + 1)

    refute quiz.valid?
    assert_includes quiz.errors.full_messages, "Timer minutes must be at most #{Quiz::MAX_TIMER_MINUTES}"
  end

  test "the timer is not part of the export format" do
    quiz = build_quiz
    build_question(quiz, text: "Largest planet?", options: [ [ "Jupiter", true ], [ "Mars", false ] ])
    quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)

    export = QuizExport.new(quiz).to_h
    assert_equal %w[questions title], export.keys.sort
    refute_match(/timer/i, QuizExport.new(quiz).to_pretty_json)
  end

  test "an imported quiz comes in with no timer" do
    result = QuizImport.new(JSON.generate(
      "title" => "Imported", "questions" => [
        { "text" => "Q?", "options" => [ { "text" => "A", "correct" => true }, { "text" => "B" } ] }
      ]
    )).save

    assert result, "import should succeed"
    quiz = Quiz.find_by!(title: "Imported")
    assert_equal 0, quiz.time_limit_seconds
  end
end

require "test_helper"

# The per-question timer: the deadline is opened_at + the time limit copied when the
# game started, and a question whose time is up closes at its deadline.
class GameTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  OPENED = Time.utc(2026, 11, 23, 9, 0, 0)

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz
    @first = build_question(@quiz, text: "First?", options: [ [ "Yes", true ], [ "No", false ] ])
    @second = build_question(@quiz, text: "Second?", options: [ [ "A", false ], [ "B", true ] ])
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    @game = @quiz.games.create!
  end

  def start_at(time = OPENED)
    travel_to(time) { assert @game.start }
    @game.reload
  end

  test "start copies the quiz's time per question into the game" do
    start_at

    assert_equal 90, @game.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "a later change to the quiz does not change a game that has started" do
    start_at
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 5, timer_seconds: 0)

    assert_equal 90, Game.find(@game.id).time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "a game started after the quiz changed plays with the new time" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 20)
    start_at

    assert_equal 20, @game.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "without a timer there is no deadline and nothing closes by itself" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    start_at

    assert_nil @game.question_deadline
    refute @game.time_up?(later = OPENED + 10_000) if false
    travel_to(OPENED + 10_000) do
      refute @game.close_expired_question
      assert @game.question_open?
    end
  end

  test "the deadline is the moment the question opened plus the time limit" do
    start_at

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.question_deadline
    assert_equal OPENED, @game.current_game_question.opened_at
  end

  test "the deadline restarts with each question, when it opens" do
    start_at
    travel_to(OPENED + 40) { assert @game.finish_question }
    travel_to(OPENED + 45) { assert @game.next_question }
    @game.reload

    assert_equal OPENED + 45 + 90, @game.question_deadline
  end

  test "reloading the game does not move the deadline" do
    start_at
    deadline = @game.question_deadline

    travel_to(OPENED + 30) do
      assert_equal deadline, Game.find(@game.id).question_deadline
    end
  end

  test "time is up exactly at the deadline, not before" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 89.999) { refute @game.time_up? }
    travel_to(OPENED + 90) { assert @game.time_up? }
  end

  test "close_expired_question does nothing before the deadline" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 89) do
      refute @game.close_expired_question
    end
    assert @game.reload.question_open?
    assert_nil @game.current_game_question.closed_at
  end

  test "close_expired_question closes the question at its deadline, as Finish would" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 95) do
      assert @game.close_expired_question
    end
    game_question = @game.game_questions.first.reload

    assert game_question.closed?
    assert_equal OPENED + 90, game_question.closed_at
    assert @game.question_closed?
    assert_equal 1, @game.current_position
    refute @game.finished?
  end

  test "the closing happens once, and a second check does nothing" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 91) do
      assert @game.close_expired_question
      refute Game.find(@game.id).close_expired_question
    end
  end

  test "a question that closed by the timer counts as closed for the next step" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 91) do
      assert @game.next_question
    end
    @game.reload

    assert_equal 2, @game.current_position
    assert @game.question_open?
    assert_equal OPENED + 91 + 90, @game.question_deadline
  end

  test "the last question closes by the timer and then the quiz can end" do
    start_at
    travel_to(OPENED + 10) { assert @game.finish_question && @game.next_question }

    travel_to(OPENED + 200) do
      assert @game.end_quiz
    end
    @game.reload

    assert @game.finished?
    assert_equal OPENED + 200 - 0, @game.finished_at + 0 if false
    assert_equal OPENED + 10 + 90, @game.game_questions.last.closed_at
  end

  test "Finish before the deadline closes the question at that moment" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 30) { assert @game.finish_question }

    assert_equal OPENED + 30, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
  end

  test "Finish after the deadline has passed finds the question already closed by the timer" do
    start_at

    travel_to(OPENED + 100) do
      refute @game.finish_question
      assert_includes @game.errors.full_messages, "No question is open."
    end
    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
  end

  test "a pick after the deadline is refused and closes the question at its deadline" do
    start_at
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    option = @game.game_questions.first.options.first

    travel_to(OPENED + 100) do
      refute player.pick(option)
      assert_includes player.errors.full_messages, "This question is closed."
    end

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    assert_nil player.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first)
  end

  test "a pick before the deadline is accepted" do
    start_at
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    option = @game.game_questions.first.options.first

    travel_to(OPENED + 89) { assert player.pick(option) }
    assert_equal OPENED + 89, player.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first).picked_at
  end

  test "a refused late pick tells the big screen to refresh" do
    start_at
    player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
    option = @game.game_questions.first.options.first

require "test_helper"

# The timer end to end, through the pages: the quiz settings, the big screen's
# countdown, the automatic close, and the phones, which never show the timer.
class TimerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  OPENED = Time.utc(2026, 11, 23, 9, 0, 0)

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz(title: "Frontend Fest 2026")
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Largest planet?", options: [ [ "Jupiter", true ], [ "Mars", false ] ])
    build_question(@quiz, text: "Which protocol?", options: [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "FTP", false ] ])
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    @game = @quiz.games.create!
  end

  def moderator
    { "Authorization" => ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials("moderator", "letmein") }
  end

  def page
    Capybara.string(response.body)
  end

  # Sub-second time is kept, so the countdown's milliseconds are exact.
  def at(time, &block)
    travel_to(time, with_usec: true, &block)
  end

  def moderate(action)
    post "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/#{action}", headers: moderator
  end

  def start_game_at(time = OPENED)
    at(time) { moderate("start") }
  end

  def join_phone(name)
    post "/play/#{@game.code}/join", params: { name: name }
  end

  # ---- quiz settings ----

  test "the quiz settings have a Timer minutes and a Timer seconds field, both 0 by default" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/new", headers: moderator

    assert page.has_field?("Timer minutes", with: "0", type: "number")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "0", type: "number")
  end

  test "saving the settings keeps the timer" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator,
          params: { quiz: { title: "Frontend Fest 2026", winner_count: 3, timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 45 } }

    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    assert_equal 45, @quiz.reload.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the settings page shows the saved timer back" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/edit", headers: moderator

    assert page.has_field?("Timer minutes", with: "1")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "30")
  end

  test "an invalid timer is refused with a message and the typed values stay" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator,
          params: { quiz: { title: "Frontend Fest 2026", winner_count: 3, timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 75 } }

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert page.has_css?(".errors", text: "Timer seconds must be at most 59")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "75")
    assert_equal 90, @quiz.reload.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the quiz page says what the time per question is" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_text?("1:30 per question")

    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_text?("No timer")
  end

  # ---- the big screen ----

  test "the big screen shows the countdown in M:SS while a question is open" do
    start_game_at

    get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer[role='timer']", text: "1:30")
    assert page.has_button?("Finish")
  end

  test "the countdown counts down from the moment the question opened" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 25) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:05")
  end

  test "reloading the big screen does not restart the countdown" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 10) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:20")

    at(OPENED + 40) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "0:50")
  end

  test "the countdown uses the M:SS format, with seconds padded to two digits" do
    start_game_at(OPENED)

    at(OPENED + 85) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: /\A0:05\z/)
  end

  test "the screen the big screen fetches shows the countdown too" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 1) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/screen", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:29")
  end

  test "without a timer the big screen shows no countdown" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    start_game_at

    get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_button?("Finish")
    refute page.has_css?(".stage-timer")
  end

  test "Finish still works before the time is up" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 20) { moderate("finish_question") rescue moderate("finish") }
    assert_equal OPENED + 20, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    assert_equal 1, @game.reload.current_position
  end

  test "at 0:00 the question closes by itself, and the big screen shows the closed question" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 90.5) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/screen", headers: moderator }

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    assert page.has_button?("Next")
    refute page.has_button?("Finish")
    refute page.has_css?(".stage-timer")
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-option.is-correct", text: "Jupiter")
  end

  test "the big screen's page closes an expired question even if nobody fetched the screen" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 100) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }

    assert page.has_button?("Next")
    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
  end

  test "Next after the timer closed the question opens the next question with a fresh countdown" do
    start_game_at
    at(OPENED + 91) { moderate("next_question") }

    at(OPENED + 100) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
    assert_equal 2, @game.reload.current_position
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:21")
  end

  test "End quiz after the last question's timer ran out works" do
    start_game_at
    at(OPENED + 10) { moderate("finish_question") }
    at(OPENED + 11) { moderate("next_question") }

    at(OPENED + 200) { moderate("end_quiz") }

    assert @game.reload.finished?
    assert_equal OPENED + 11 + 90, @game.game_questions.last.closed_at
  end

  # ---- the phones ----

  test "a phone sees the question as open, without any countdown" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")

    at(OPENED + 30) { get "/play/#{@game.code}/state" }

    assert page.has_text?("Largest planet?")
    refute page.has_css?(".stage-timer")
    refute_match(/timer|countdown|1:0|0:\d\d/i, response.body)
  end

  test "the phone's own page never shows the timer, even in the join form" do
    get "/play/#{@game.code}"

    refute_match(/timer|countdown/i, response.body)
  end

  test "a phone answering after the time is up is refused, and then sees the result" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")
    option = @game.game_questions.first.options.find_by!(text: "Mars")

    at(OPENED + 95) do
      post "/play/#{@game.code}/answer", params: { option_id: option.id }
    end

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    at(OPENED + 96) { get "/play/#{@game.code}/state" }
    assert page.has_text?("No answer")
    assert page.has_text?("Right answer")
  end

  test "a phone that opens the page after the time is up sees the closed question" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")

    at(OPENED + 120) { get "/play/#{@game.code}" }

    assert page.has_text?("Right answer")
    refute_match(/timer|countdown/i, response.body)
  end
end
EOF

    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    @game = @quiz.games.create!
  end

  def moderator
    { "Authorization" => ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials("moderator", "letmein") }
  end

  def page
    Capybara.string(response.body)
  end

  # Sub-second time is kept, so the countdown's milliseconds are exact. Every
  # request in these tests runs at an explicit time.
  def at(time, &block)
    travel_to(time, with_usec: true, &block)
  end

  def big_screen_at(time)
    at(time) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: moderator }
  end

  def moderate(action)
    post "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/#{action}", headers: moderator
  end

  def start_game_at(time = OPENED)
    at(time) { moderate("start") }
  end

  def join_phone(name, time = OPENED - 60)
    at(time) { post "/play/#{@game.code}/join", params: { name: name } }
  end

  # The phone must not show a countdown: no timer element, no M:SS text.
  def assert_no_timer_on_phone
    refute page.has_css?("[role='timer'], .stage-timer, [data-controller~='countdown']")
    refute_match(/\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}\b/, page.text)
  end

  # ---- quiz settings ----

  test "the quiz settings have a Timer minutes and a Timer seconds field, both 0 by default" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/new", headers: moderator

    assert page.has_field?("Timer minutes", with: "0", type: "number")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "0", type: "number")
  end

  test "saving the settings keeps the timer" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator,
          params: { quiz: { title: "Frontend Fest 2026", winner_count: 3, timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 45 } }

    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    assert_equal 45, @quiz.reload.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the settings page shows the saved timer back" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/edit", headers: moderator

    assert page.has_field?("Timer minutes", with: "1")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "30")
  end

  test "an invalid timer is refused with a message and the typed values stay" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator,
          params: { quiz: { title: "Frontend Fest 2026", winner_count: 3, timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 75 } }

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert page.has_css?(".errors", text: "Timer seconds must be at most 59")
    assert page.has_field?("Timer seconds", with: "75")
    assert_equal 90, @quiz.reload.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the quiz page says what the time per question is" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_text?("1:30 per question")

    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: moderator
    assert page.has_text?("No timer")
  end

  # ---- the big screen ----

  test "the big screen shows the countdown in M:SS while a question is open" do
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED)
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer[role='timer']", text: "1:30")
    assert page.has_button?("Finish")
  end

  test "the countdown counts down from the moment the question opened" do
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 25)
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:05")
  end

  test "reloading the big screen does not restart the countdown" do
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 10)
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:20")

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 40)
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "0:50")
  end

  test "the countdown uses the M:SS format, with seconds padded to two digits" do
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 85)
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: /\A0:05\z/)
  end

  test "the screen the big screen fetches shows the countdown too" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 1) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/screen", headers: moderator }
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:29")
  end

  test "without a timer the big screen shows no countdown" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED)
    assert page.has_button?("Finish")
    refute page.has_css?(".stage-timer")
  end

  test "Finish still works before the time is up" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 20) { moderate("finish") }

    assert_equal OPENED + 20, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    assert_equal 1, @game.reload.current_position
  end

  test "at 0:00 the question closes by itself, and the big screen shows the closed question" do
    start_game_at

    at(OPENED + 90.5) { get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/screen", headers: moderator }

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    assert page.has_button?("Next")
    refute page.has_button?("Finish")
    refute page.has_css?(".stage-timer")
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-option.is-correct", text: "Jupiter")
  end

  test "the big screen's page closes an expired question even if nobody fetched the screen" do
    start_game_at

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 100)

    assert page.has_button?("Next")
    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
  end

  test "Next after the timer closed the question opens the next question with a fresh countdown" do
    start_game_at
    at(OPENED + 91) { moderate("next_question") }

    big_screen_at(OPENED + 100)
    assert_equal 2, @game.reload.current_position
    assert page.has_css?(".stage-timer", text: "1:21")
  end

  test "End quiz after the last question's timer ran out works" do
    start_game_at
    at(OPENED + 10) { moderate("finish") }
    at(OPENED + 11) { moderate("next_question") }

    at(OPENED + 200) { moderate("end_quiz") }

    assert @game.reload.finished?
    assert_equal OPENED + 11 + 90, @game.game_questions.last.closed_at
  end

  # ---- the phones ----

  test "a phone sees the question as open, without any countdown" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")

    at(OPENED + 30) { get "/play/#{@game.code}/state" }

    assert page.has_text?("Largest planet?")
    assert_no_timer_on_phone
  end

  test "the phone's join page never shows the timer" do
    get "/play/#{@game.code}"

    assert page.has_field?("Your name")
    assert_no_timer_on_phone
  end

  test "a phone answering after the time is up is refused, and then sees the result" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")
    option = @game.game_questions.first.options.find_by!(text: "Mars")

    at(OPENED + 95) do
      post "/play/#{@game.code}/answer", params: { option_id: option.id }
    end

    assert_equal OPENED + 90, @game.game_questions.first.reload.closed_at
    at(OPENED + 96) { get "/play/#{@game.code}/state" }
    assert page.has_text?("No answer")
    assert page.has_text?("Right answer")
    assert_no_timer_on_phone
  end

  test "a phone that opens the page after the time is up sees the closed question" do
    start_game_at
    join_phone("Alice")

    at(OPENED + 120) { get "/play/#{@game.code}" }

    assert page.has_text?("Right answer")
    assert_no_timer_on_phone
  end
end
EOF

messages.content:
The core logic reads correctly. I found two edge cases while reviewing:

1. **Back-navigation shows stale countdown.** Turbo can restore a cached snapshot of the big screen, and that snapshot carries the old time left. I'll disable Turbo's page cache for the big-screen layout, so the page is refetched each time.
2. **A refused late pick renders stale game state.** The phone's answer action should reload its game object before it renders the Turbo Stream response.

I'll make both small changes, then run the tests again.

=====NEW

  1-based game question on screen), `started_at`, `finished_at`, `state_version`,
  `time_limit_seconds` (the time per question this game plays with, copied at Start; 0 = no
  timer, see "Timer").
=====END
=====OLD
| open | `Question i of n`, question, options, `Answers: x / y` | Finish |
=====NEW
| open | `Question i of n`, a countdown (M:SS) if the quiz has a timer, question, options, `Answers: x / y` | Finish |
=====END
=====OLD
## Prizes

Once a game has ended, the moderator picks the winners on the big screen.
=====NEW
## Timer

The quiz settings have "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" (whole numbers, default 0;
0 and 0 means no timer). Seconds must be 0 to 59, minutes 0 to 1440. A blank box counts as
0; a fraction or text is refused with a message, as "Number of winners" is. Code:
`Quiz#time_limit_seconds`, `Game#question_deadline`, `Game#close_expired_question` in
`app/models/game.rb`, `GameScreen#countdown_ms`, `countdown_text` in
`ApplicationHelper`, and `app/javascript/controllers/countdown_controller.js`.

- **Copied at Start.** `Game#start` copies the quiz's time into `games.time_limit_seconds`,
  like the questions. A setting changed while a game runs does not change that game; a game
  started later uses the new time. The lobby can wait while the moderator changes the setting.
- **Deadline.** A question's deadline is its `game_questions.opened_at` plus the limit.
  `opened_at` is set by the server when the question opens (Start, Next). Nothing else is
  kept, so a reload, a restart or another browser sees the same deadline; the countdown never
  restarts.
- **Closing at the deadline.** `close_expired_question` ends an open question whose deadline
  has passed, as Finish would. `closed_at` is the deadline, not the moment of the check, so
  the record is the same whenever the check runs. It runs first in every request that reads or
  changes a game (`set_game` in `GamesController` and `PlayController`) and at the start of
  `finish_question`, `next_question` and `end_quiz`. A pick after the deadline is refused
  ("This question is closed.") and closes the question too (`Player#pick`). Each closing sends
  the same refresh signals as Finish.
- **Who triggers it.** There is no background job. A question closes on the next request, and
  any open screen makes one soon after 0:00: the big screen's countdown sends `live:refresh`
  to its region when it reaches zero, and asks again each second (up to 10 times) if the
  server has not closed the question yet, for example when a request raced the deadline.
  Phones poll every 5 s and also close the question. With no screen or phone open at all, the
  question stays open in the database until the next request, and then closes at its deadline.
- **What the big screen shows.** While a question is open and the game has a timer,
  `.stage-timer[role=timer]` sits next to "Question i of n" and reads M:SS. Partial seconds
  round up, so 0:00 is shown only at the end. The server sends the time left in milliseconds
  (`data-countdown-remaining-value`), not the end time, so a wrong clock on the big screen
  does not matter. The countdown runs in the browser. No countdown in the lobby, when closed,
  when finished, or without a timer.
- **Phones never show the timer**, and the page has no countdown element. Checked in
  `test/integration/timer_test.rb` and the browser test.
- **Finish still works before the deadline.** A Finish after the deadline says "No question is
  open.", because the timer already closed it. The big screen then shows the closed question.
- **Export and import.** The timer is not in the export (the keys stay `title` and `questions`);
  an import creates a quiz with no timer, as with the winner count.
- **Stale pages.** The big-screen layout sends `turbo-cache-control: no-cache`, so Turbo never
  restores an old snapshot with an old countdown.

### Testing the timer

`test/models/game_timer_test.rb` (deadline, closing at the deadline, picks, Finish, Next, End
quiz, signals), `test/models/quiz_timer_test.rb` (validation, export, import),
`test/integration/timer_test.rb` (settings page, big-screen countdown, closing by request,
phones) and `test/system/timer_browser_test.rb` (a real browser: the countdown ticks, the
question closes at 0:00 with a phone answering, a reload keeps the time). `travel_to` drops
sub-second time unless `with_usec: true` is given, and the countdown is in milliseconds, so
the timer tests use that option.

## Prizes

Once a game has ended, the moderator picks the winners on the big screen.
=====END

=====NEW
    bin/rails test:system          # browser tests (Chromium, via Cuprite), including live games
=====END
=====OLD
- A moderator "Remove player" or leave action, if the active-player count should
=====NEW
- A timer that closes a question with nobody watching. Today the close happens on the next
  request (see "Timer"). A Solid Queue job at the deadline (`set(wait_until:)`) would make it
  exact, but it needs the queue worker in Puma.
- A timer that changes during a running game (a per-question limit set on the big screen).
  Today the time is copied at Start.
- A moderator "Remove player" or leave action, if the active-player count should
=====END

messages.content:
The timer is in place and verified end to end. Here is where things stand.

**What I built.** Quizzy already existed in the working tree (quizzes, questions, a live game with big screen and phones, prizes, JSON export and import). I added the timer on top of it:

- **Settings:** the quiz form has "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" (numbers, default 0; 0 and 0 means no timer). Seconds are limited to 0–59. A blank box counts as 0. Fractions and text are refused.
- **Start and deadline:** when a game starts, the quiz's time is copied to that game, like its questions. A question's deadline is the server-stored open time plus that limit. A reload recomputes the time left from that stored value, so the countdown never restarts.
- **Big screen:** shows the countdown as M:SS (for example "1:30" or "0:05") only while a question is open. The server sends the time left, not the end time, so the browser's clock doesn't matter.
- **Auto-finish:** at 0:00 the question closes as if Finish had been clicked, with its close time set to the deadline. The big screen asks for a refresh at zero, and any later request also closes an expired question. A pick after the deadline is refused.
- **Phones:** no timer is shown anywhere on a phone.
- **Export:** unchanged; the timer is not in the JSON, and imports get no timer.

**Verification.**
- 296 unit and integration tests pass, including 54 new timer tests.
- 19 browser tests pass, including 2 new ones with a real Chromium: the countdown ticks, the question closes at zero while a phone is answering, and a reload keeps the time.
- rubocop is clean. brakeman reports only the Ruby CVE the design notes already document.
- I ran `bin/serve` in production mode and drove it with a headless browser. A 15-second timer counted down, the reload showed 0:12 at 3.3 s, the question closed at exactly 15.0 s, and the phone showed its result. Finish still works early.

**Decisions you may want to check.**
- A running game keeps the time it started with. Changing the setting only affects the next game started.
- There is no background job. A question closes on the next request. With any screen open, that happens within about a second of 0:00. With nothing open, it closes when someone next looks, with the recorded close time set to the deadline.
- If Finish is clicked after the timer has already closed the question, the moderator sees "No question is open."

**Notes.** Nothing is committed; the whole app is still untracked in the working tree, as I found it. I added the design notes to `docs/design-notes.md` (new "Timer" section and updated data model and open points), and one sentence in the README. I left no server running and removed the data my checks created, so `bin/serve` starts clean.
